newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Ryan Hotels says profits ahead of last yr.
newsitem.headline: Ryan Hotels says profits ahead of last yr.

text.p: Ryan Hotels Plc said on Tuesday that the new financial year had started well with profits to date running ahead of last year.

The group, which announced pre-tax profits of 4.04 million Irish pounds for the year ended January 30, 1997, said its policy of investing in its existing properties and changing the mix of its business to high margin activities had resulted in the 45 percent rise in profits.
Trading margins improved to 22 percent from 19 percent resulting in an increase of 19 percent to six million punts in trading profit, Ryan said in a statement.
Both its continental and Irish hotels contributed to the growth in profit, Ryan said.
Corporate activity in the Gresham and the Royal Marine hotels in Dublin was at an all-time high while demand was strong at the Galway Ryan which added an extensive leisure centre in 1995.
Ryan said it had completed the first phase of an enhancement programme and had spent 4.1 million Irish pounds, charged against the profit and loss account, over the last four years.
The company was now at a stage where it needed to increase its bedroom stock to cater for the growing demand from its customers, Ryan said.
"We plan to do this initially by adding to existing hotel properties," it said.
Work will commence shortly on the development of a 100-bedroom extension of the Gresham Hotel along with a 150 space multi-storey car park.
A feasibility study on a bedroom extension to the Galway Ryan is being undertaken and the group will apply for planning permission shortly.

The group said it spent 25,000 punts a week on refurbishment, replacement and maintenance during the year, a 25 percent increase, but still managed to reduce its debt by 2.5 million Irish pounds leaving it with net debt, excluding leasing obligations, of 34 percent of shareholders' funds.
"The strong improvement in trading should enable us to carry out these developments and still maintain our debt/equity ratio at current levels," Ryan said.
